channel.title: Chain Times
channel.description: Chain Times reports crypto news: bitcoin and ether markets, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: EU proposal targets Russian banks and crypto networks
item.description: The European Commission proposed targeting 60 Russian banks and crypto networks in a new sanctions package, but all 27 EU states must approve it.

item.title: EVM Compatibility: What Carries Across Chains
item.description: What does EVM compatible mean for a blockchain? It means Ethereum contracts, wallets and addresses can work across chains that run the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

item.title: DEX router contract: What happens in a swap
item.description: A router contract in a DEX swap takes your tokens, routes them through pools, checks the minimum output and sends you the result—or reverts in one transaction.

item.title: EU targets crypto networks in proposed Russia sanctions
item.description: The European Commission has proposed a 22nd Russia sanctions package that targets crypto and payment networks, with a new task force to support enforcement.

item.title: How do you move Bitcoin to an Ethereum L2? Wrapped BTC
item.description: To move Bitcoin to an Ethereum layer 2, use a BTC-backed token: withdraw it to the network or bridge it from Ethereum, then check the balance in your L2 wallet.

item.title: Chainflip puts vault theft at about $12 million, offers 10% bounty
item.description: Chainflip says an attacker took 122.86 BTC alongside ETH and stablecoins, lifting disclosed losses to about $12 million; it offered a 10% bounty for most of the funds’ return.

item.title: MoonPay seeks OCC charter for trust bank and stablecoin services
item.description: MoonPay has asked the OCC to charter a national trust bank for custody and stablecoin services, a move that could place those plans under federal oversight.

item.title: Coinbase brings Morpho-backed crypto loans to New York
item.description: Coinbase Borrow is now available to New York residents, who can borrow USDC against bitcoin, ether or solana through Morpho on Base.

item.title: CFTC chief says Hyperliquid must follow the same exchange rules
item.description: CFTC Chair Michael Selig said onchain venues need exchange approval or a registered partner to offer derivatives to U.S. retail traders, with no special rules for blockchain platforms.

item.title: cBridge Pool Transfers and Destination Liquidity
item.description: When a bridge pool does not have enough liquidity, cBridge blocks the quote or refunds a transfer it cannot pay from the destination pool in full.

item.title: DBS and Circle open 24/7 USDC access for Asian institutions
item.description: DBS and Circle say eligible institutions in Asia can mint and redeem USDC through the bank at any hour, adding a direct route beyond secondary markets.

item.title: Is bridging crypto between networks a taxable event? Swap cases
item.description: Bridging the same asset between your own wallets is often not taxable. Swaps, wrapped tokens and gas paid in crypto can change the result by country.

item.title: ETH for DEX Token Swaps: How Gas Works
item.description: Why do I need ETH to swap tokens on a DEX? Each swap needs the chain’s native coin for gas, and a first token trade may need both an approval and a swap.

item.title: Token Approval Revocation: Checking the Allowance
item.description: To check if a token approval was revoked, wait for confirmation, then read the ERC-20 allowance for your wallet and spender on the same network; zero means none remains.

item.title: Sent transaction: Why Etherscan can’t find it yet
item.description: Why does a sent transaction not show up on Etherscan? A hash can exist before any node accepts it; private routing can keep it off the public tracker.

item.title: Bridge relayer after tokens are locked: how delivery works
item.description: What does a bridge relayer do after tokens are locked? It waits for finality and attestation, then submits the message that completes delivery.

item.title: How to Revoke Token Approvals in MetaMask After Trading to Zero
item.description: How to revoke token approvals in MetaMask after trading: submit a zero-allowance transaction through a chain-compatible approval manager, then verify it.

item.title: deBridge vs Across: Pick the Cheaper Route for This Transfer
item.description: deBridge vs Across: Across usually costs less for small, same-token moves; deBridge can win on large transfers or swaps. Compare live quotes by amount received.

item.title: Polygon bridge: how transfers work and what to check
item.description: Polygon bridge explained for beginners: it locks supported tokens on Ethereum and mints matching tokens on Polygon PoS, then reverses the process for withdrawals.

item.title: Short liquidity locks: match the term to your holding period
item.description: A short liquidity lock restricts LP withdrawal only until its release time, so compare the time left with your planned holding period to judge token rug risk.
